title: ANDS Studio — Dossier catalog / workspace home
walkthrough:
The page opens with a demo notice strip: "Demo / evaluation environment — nothing here is transmitted to Health Canada and no email is sent." Below it a top navigation bar shows a dot and "ANDS Studio · dossier manager", then icon-and-label chips linking to Journey, Dossiers, Portfolio, Registry, Correspondence, and Help; the active one is highlighted, with a user chip at the far right. If not yet dismissed, a "What you'll do here" primer appears, tagged "New to ANDS? Start here", with a link to the guided Journey and a "Got it" button.

The heading "Your product dossiers" sits beside a Grid / List view toggle, a "View archived (trash)" button, and a "New dossier +" button. An explanatory paragraph states that a Dossier ID is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada, that opening a dossier lets you build its eCTD Module 1–5, and that client workspaces are isolated end-to-end. Several terms carry glossary tooltips. With none yet, a notice reads "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission."

Clicking "New dossier +" (which toggles to "Cancel") opens an inline card with fields for Dossier ID (placeholder "e123456"), Product name, a Submission type dropdown (ANDS, SANDS, SNDS), and optional Client / sponsor and Owner (PM). On the ANDS default a "Comparative-BE only (CS-BE path…)" checkbox shows. Small print explains that Health Canada issues the Dossier ID via a Dossier ID Request through REP; a link-style "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →" auto-fills a generated draft ID. Pressing "Create & open →" with an invalid ID shows a red notice: "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)"; on success a toast confirms creation and you enter the dossier's Module 1 workspace.

Once dossiers exist, a triage bar offers a filter input ("Filter by product, ID, type, client or owner…"), a "Just my dossiers" checkbox, and a count of shown-of-total. In Grid view each dossier is a clickable tile: its ID, product title, a meta line (submission type, CS-BE when applicable, sponsor), a progress bar, and a status chip. The chip never claims filing readiness — it reads "N/N modules built — validate to file" or just "N/N modules built", with a tooltip noting this is structural completeness only, not a validation pass. Placeholder dossiers carry a "⚠ placeholder — set real ID ✎" chip warning that export and transmission are blocked until the real ID is set; each tile has a "✕" delete button. List view shows a sortable table with Dossier ID, Product, Status, Type, Client / sponsor, Owner, and Soonest due, with overdue dates flagged.

Clicking delete opens a "Delete this dossier?" modal explaining the dossier is archived rather than destroyed and recorded on the audit trail; you type the Dossier ID and a required reason before "Archive dossier" enables. The placeholder chip opens "Set the real Health Canada Dossier ID", where you enter a new ID and reason, then "Apply new ID". "View archived (trash)" reveals an "Archived (recoverable)" list showing when and by whom each was archived, with a "Restore ↩" button. Delete and restore raise confirming toasts.
